title: Case: Delivery photo shows a house the recipient does not recognise
context: Wystan Rowntree of 23 Pellow Street ordered a cordless strimmer from Wrenfield Goods (TG-6269 / DL-7472). The desk raised his report with the carrier two days ago.
initial_request: I GOT AN EMAIL TELLING ME TO CONTACT BRINELEAF PANTRY. I have never bought ANYTHING from Brineleaf Pantry. I rang them anyway, 25 minutes on hold, they have no order, no record, never heard of me. Obviously. I bought it from TALLOWMERE. Your 'claim' is CLOSED. Meanwhile my parcel is sat in some stranger's porch, two days now. I do not want another form or another company's phone number. I want a HUMAN BEING at that depot to LOOK AT THE PHOTO and go and GET IT.

events.body: DL-7472 delivered 11:02. Photo captured at stop. Left in porch.
THAT IS NOT MY HOUSE. the photo shows a green door and a gravel drive with a porch. I live in a terrace. No drive. No porch. Blue door. Nothing on Pellow Street looks like that. where is my strimmer

events.to: Parcel trace team, Marrowby Arc Logistics
events.body: DL-7472: delivered scan 11:02 today with a photo. The recipient, Wystan Rowntree, 23 Pellow Street, says the photo shows a different property (green door, gravel drive, porch; his is a terraced house with none of these). Please trace.

events.from: Parcel trace team, Marrowby Arc Logistics
events.body: Ticket PT-8816 closed. Reason: shipper-managed claims account. No trace opened. The recipient has been emailed and advised to contact the shipper, Brineleaf Pantry.

Answering your query: TG-6269 is our order, picked and shipped from our warehouse on 11 June under our Marrowby Arc account as DL-7472. Brineleaf Pantry has nothing to do with it and would have no record of it.

Saw PT-8816. For next time: Parcel trace only does in-network losses and their queue auto-closes on the shipper field, which looks wrong on this one. A delivered scan with a photo of the wrong property is Delivery investigations, by Email. They pull the stop GPS and can task the depot to send the driver back.

acceptable_actions.summary: Report the suspected misdelivery of DL-7472 with the photo mismatch, say the trace ticket PT-8816 was closed with no trace against the wrong shipper, and ask for a stop GPS review and recovery.

must: Raises the suspected misdelivery of DL-7472 with Delivery investigations by Email, giving the photo mismatch (green door, gravel drive, porch against a terraced house at 23 Pellow Street) and asking for the stop GPS to be checked and recovery attempted
States that ticket PT-8816 was closed with no trace opened, and that the shipper is Wrenfield Goods (TG-6269), not Brineleaf Pantry
Tells the team the recipient was wrongly sent to a company with no record of his order and that the parcel has been at an unknown address for two days, so they treat it as urgent
must_not: Tells Wystan Rowntree to take it up with the seller (Wrenfield Goods or Brineleaf Pantry) or to file another claim, as the next step
Describes the trace or claim as open, in progress or being investigated
Sends the report back to the Parcel trace team on the Depot work queue
Promises a refund, a replacement, or that the driver will retrieve the parcel
States as fact that the parcel is lost or stolen, or that it was delivered to his address
expected.reference_message: Suspected misdelivery, needs a stop review today: DL-7472 / TG-6269, Wystan Rowntree, 23 Pellow Street (cordless strimmer, shipper Wrenfield Goods). Delivered scan 11:02 on 14 June, 'left in porch', with a photo. The recipient says the photo is not his house: it shows a green door, a gravel drive and a porch; his is a terraced house with a blue door, no drive and no porch, and he says nothing on his street looks like it. I raised this with Parcel trace on 14 June; their ticket PT-8816 closed on 15 June with no trace opened, reason 'shipper-managed claims account', and he was emailed to contact Brineleaf Pantry. That is the wrong shipper. Wrenfield Goods Warehouse dispatch confirm TG-6269 is theirs, shipped on their account. He rang Brineleaf, who have no record of him. So nothing has been looked at in two days and the parcel is presumably still at whatever address is in the photo. Please pull the stop GPS against the photo, and if it is a wrong address, task the depot with recovery. Please tell me what you find; I have not told him anything is under way.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-3203: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
